title: bugfix: check_linker_flag cache-variable reuse
body:
`check_linker_flag(LANG FLAGS VAR)` stores its result in `VAR` as a cache variable (see [CheckLinkerFlag](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/module/CheckLinkerFlag.html)). On any later call where VAR already exists in the cache, CMake short-circuits and skips the actual linker probe, reusing the previous verdict.

I discovered this while trying to use LLD linker on AArch64. It kept failing on `--stub-group-size=0x2000000` which if the logic worked properly shouldn't have been applied by CMake to the linker command. It was applied because the `_supported` var was cached from the previous call to `check_linker_flag`.

This commit changes the `add_link_options_if_supported` (which calls `check_linker_flag`) to take a variable name from the user.

CMake now prints this when it encounters an unsupported flag:
```
CMake Warning at cmake/public/utils.cmake:553 (message):
  Attempted to use unsupported link option : --stub-group-size=0x2000000.
```
